I decided to learn how to cook last summer, mostly because I was tired of eating takeout every single night. My first attempt was scrambled eggs, which sounds pathetic, I know. But honestly? I burned them. Not a little — I mean I had to open every window in the apartment.

My mom sent me her recipe for chicken soup over text. The instructions were maddeningly vague. "Add some salt" — how much salt, Mom? "Cook until it looks right" — what does right even look like? I called her three times during the process. She was patient, mostly.

The soup turned out okay. Not great, not terrible. My roommate said it tasted like something, which I chose to take as a compliment. The next week I tried pasta from scratch. Rolling out the dough was actually kind of meditative, though my arms were sore for two days afterward.

Gradually things started clicking. I learned that garlic burns fast if you're not paying attention. I figured out that sharp knives are actually safer than dull ones, which seems counterintuitive. I discovered that I actually enjoy the process — the chopping, the stirring, even the cleanup.

Now I cook most nights. Nothing fancy. Stir fries, soups, sometimes a roast on Sundays. I still mess things up regularly. Last Tuesday I accidentally used cinnamon instead of cumin, which was... an experience. But I'm getting better, and that feels pretty good.
